thread.title: Tech Today: Microsoft's New High, Amazon Number One, Skyworks Sags - Barron's

title: Tech Today: Microsoft's New High, Amazon Number One, Skyworks Sags - Barron's
text:
Updated July 20, 2018 12:09 p.m. ET
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech : Microsoft at New All-Time High
Shares of Microsoft ( MSFT ) are up $2.75, or 2.6%, to $107.15, hitting a new all-time high earlier this morning of $108.20, pushing its market capitalization to $841.3 billion, after the company yesterday afternoon beat fiscal Q4 expectations and also forecast this quarter’s revenue higher.
I see no ratings changes this morning, but prices targets are going higher at numerous shops. One the upbeat individuals is Goldman Sachs ’s Heather Bellini , who reiterates a Buy rating on the shares, and raises her price target to $125 from $114, writing the "results were strong across the board."
She notes that sales growth of server software products and of cloud computing were the “highest pace on record."
Microsoft is benefitting from letting people move over their traditional licenses for software to Microsoft’s cloud, "as partners highlight enterprise agreement renewals at higher net expansion levels than in recent years."
But the highest price targets today come from Deutsche Bank ’s Karl Keirstead and Piper Jaffray ’s Alex Zukin , who both raised the stock to $130.
Keirstead credits not only Microsoft’s “strong execution” and its “traction” in cloud computing, but also "a very healthy overall corporate IT spending backdrop."
Keirstead estimates Azure is now bringing in $10 billion annually in revenue at its current rate of growth. He notes the company “expressed no concern with our high-60% Azure growth estimate for fiscal 2019."
Zukin notes the implied forecast for earnings per share next year is above consensus at $4.27.
Zukin is especially impressed that after " the largest sales reorg in the company's history earlier in the year,” Microsoft managed to record growth in unearned revenue of 23%.
You know who’s not that impressed? John DiFucci of Jefferies & Co., who reiterates an Underperform rating, writing that it was a “solid” quarter, but that “long-term questions” remain.
"We continue to wonder if the unprecedented Windows outperformance relative to PC shipments is sustainable,” he writes, "while also questioning the ultimate margins of Azure.” Skyworks Gives Up Gains
A name not faring as well from last night’s reports is Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ), which has given up last night’s after-market gains and is now down $5.07, or 5%, to $97.41, despite the company reporting fiscal Q3 results that topped analysts' expectations, forecasting this quarter's profit higher, and raising its quarterly dividend by 19%.
The stock weakness comes despite many accolades from the sell side.
For example, Canaccord Genuituy ’s Mike Walkley , reiterating a Buy rating, raises his price target to $115 from $110, writing that he sees plenty of opportunity for share gain at Apple ( AAPL ) and other handset makers.
"We anticipate dollar content increases with customers including Apple as Skyworks expands integrated offerings for its customer base requiring more complex integrated solutions.
"In fact, we believe Skyworks is well positioned to gain share in future iPhones particularly with competitor Qorvo ( QRVO ) moving to higher-band PADs and losing share in low-band PADs in future iPhones."
Bears are apt to point out there are still some risks to the story. Cowen & Co .’s Karl Ackerman , for example, reiterates a Market Perform rating, while raising his price target to $105 from $100, writing that management's decision to "de-emphasize” the development of "in-house BAW filters ” is a " a huge question , particularly for carrier aggregation scenarios where combining high and low bands in a tightly integrated module will become ever more important."
And Raymond James ’s Chris Caso thinks there’s not much to get excited about until 2020, when 5G wireless really takes off: "With handset unit growth flat at best, and near-term content gains modest, we expect growth to remain modest until F20, when we expect 5G to drive faster growth."
I should note that shares of competitors Qorvo and Broadcom ( AVGO ) are also lower today. Getting Ready for Faang
With some of the Faang stocks starting to report next week, analysts are tuning up their models for what to expect.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) reports results on Thursday, after market close.
Deutsche Bank’s Lloyd Walmsley, who considers the name his “Top Pick,” reiterates a Buy rating this morning, and raises his price target to $2,200 from $1,800, writing that worries about higher spending are offset by the company’s expanding empire of initiatives.
"We recognize the concerns, however modest, regarding potential for higher near-term investment in fulfillment facilities, last-mile delivery, international markets (particularly another $2B in India), AWS,” he writes.
“These concerns are far outweighed by the large and expanding TAM most recently with the acquisition of PillPack as well as the expansions into Brazil and Australia,” he continues.
He also likes the “momentum” in Amazon’s Prime membership service, and Amazon’s recent price increases there.
And, let’s not forget, " Amazon is seen as the alternative to [Alphabet's] ( GOOGL ) Google and Facebook ( FB ),” he writes.
Alphabet reports Monday afternoon, Facebook on on Wednesday, and Stifel Nicolaus ’s Scott Devitt takes the opportunity to applaud both, writing that "We are incrementally positive on our mega cap U.S. digital advertising names (FB, GOOGL) in the near term, as reasonable valuation, the potential for multiple expansion, and digital advertising growth momentum continues."
In fact, he prefers advertising plays to e-commerce "as reasonable valuation, the potential for multiple expansion, and digital advertising growth momentum continues."
He raises his price target to on Facebook to $242 from $202, writing that his "agency checks indicate continued momentum."
Amazon shares today are up $14.51, or 0.8%, to $1,827.48, while Facebook is up $2.57, or 1%, to $210.66. Amazon at the Top of the Pecking Order
Another person who has Amazon at the top of the list is Piper ’s Michael Olson , who ranks Amazon at number one this morning in his “Inaugural Faang Rank,” in which he attempts to “pick your favorite child,” given he’s got an Overweight rating on all the Faang names.
With Amazon, he’s impressed with the “massive new addressable markets that Amazon is attacking,” worth more than a trillion dollars, across grocery , pharmaceuticals, gaming and others.” He also thinks the advertising business may double this year for Amazon.
Olson considers Netflix ( NFLX ) his second choice, followed by Apple at number three, Facebook at number four, and Alphabet last.
Of Alphabet he writes, " We do not see any specific catalysts to point to in the near term, so investors will have to rely on periodic upward estimate revisions to drive the stock.
